Route shape1 (n=176) through med split path (mega_eigh_med_split): TC batched-cuBLAS back-transform + FP16-triangle 2-CTA co-residency, replacing old full mega_eigh_k in-kernel SIMT back-transform. Confirms trial-1 ncu: shape1 was occupancy-bound (40 CTAs=0.27 waves, Block Limit Shared Mem=1, occ 12.5%, No-Eligible 79.2%, barrier 34.7%). Shape 1 2460->1949us (1.26x); shape 2 (n=352) 6030->6038 FLAT; geomean 27021.7->26538.0 (-1.8%). 39/39 VALID.

Multi-CTA cluster path C=2 PB=1 for n=176 (brief primary lever: cooperative tridiag via GPC cl.sync, 80 CTAs for 40 matrices). 39/39 VALID. Shape 1 REGRESSED 1949(med)->2934us, geomean 26538->27423.6. Confirms brief-95 at n=176: per-column cl.sync + global v/p staging + threadfence (174 barriers) latency overwhelms occupancy gain -- sync is the bottleneck. med path (t2) remains best. Next: PB>1 to amortize sync count.

Cluster PB=4 (blocked tridiag, ~44 cross-cluster syncs vs 174) for n=176. 39/39 VALID. Shape 1 2934(PB1)->2918us FLAT, still >> med 1949. Multi-CTA tridiag overhead is cross-CTA DATA-MOVEMENT-bound (global v/p staging+threadfence per column), not sync-count-bound. Decisive: cooperative tridiag doesn't pay at n=176/b40 (C=2,PB in {1,4}). med path best. Pivot to per-matrix kernel cost.

Square-storage split kernel (mega_eigh_sq_split, full n*n FP16 A, branch-free) for n<=200 to shed the packed-triangle AGET branch+_tri recompute. 39/39 VALID. Shape 1 1949(med)->2191us WORSE: branch-free win offset by square trailing update writing FULL rows (2x rank-2 O(n^3) work) vs med's triangle-only (j<=i, half). geomean 26538->26785. Packed-triangle is the better tradeoff. Reverting base to med. Next: cut tridiag work (blocked panel->TC GEMM) or bisection.

Med base restored (square off, t5 regressed) + small-n Sturm-bisection iters 45->32 (n<=200, new _MEGA_SMALL_BISITERS). Twisted eigenvectors + residual gate tolerate the coarser eigenvalue. 39/39 VALID, no extra fallback. Shape 1 1949->1882us (-3.4%), shape 2 6044 FLAT (keeps 45), geomean 26538->26505.7. Bisection ~23% of the kernel; bisiters still sweepable (probe 30->1872).

Small-n CTA nt 512->256 (fewer warps at the per-column barrier ncu measured at 66%). 39/39 VALID. Shape 1 1882->1896us FLAT (noise), geomean 26505.7->26493.9 FLAT. Barrier latency is SM/GPC arrival cost with 40 CTAs 1/SM, NOT idle-warp participation -- warp-count knob doesn't cheapen it. nt=128 would double bisection critical path. Barrier wall needs structural fix (blocked panel / co-resident CTAs).

Two-slot named-barrier kernel (mega_eigh_med_split2, 2 matrices/CTA, per-slot barrier.sync id=1+g) to OVERLAP the two matrices' per-column barrier stalls (hide the 66% barrier at 40 CTAs 1/SM). 39/39 VALID (correct, compiled 10.0a). Shape 1 1882->2492us REGRESSION, geomean 26505.7->27126.4. Overlap fails: the 2 slots' 16 warps share the same 4 schedulers so a slot's barrier waits on time-sliced warps (slower, not hidden), and grid halves to 20 CTAs (20/148 SMs). Software co-residency can't hide the barrier -- needs true co-resident CTAs HW won't give at b=40. Disabling 2-slot; best remains t6 (bisIters=32, shape1 1882us).

TF32 back-transform for n<=200 (_MEGA_SMALL_BT_PREC='tf32') to move the ~14% back-transform GEMMs onto tensor cores. Threading correct, 39/39 test shapes VALID, but benchmark shape 1 1882->7877us MASS cuSOLVER fallback (TF32 ~3e-4/op error over 174-reflector WY product trips orth gate -> most matrices fall back). geomean 26505.7->29547.6. FP32-SIMT back-transform required for accuracy even at n=176. Reverting to fp32. Also disabled 2-slot (t8) and restored nt=512 (t6 winner) in this trial.

tf32x3 (Ozaki 3-pass, ~FP32 accuracy) back-transform for n<=200. 39/39 VALID, no mass fallback. Shape 1 1882->2565us regressed: back-transform is a ~18-GEMM panel loop at n=176, tf32x3 triples to ~54 small GEMM launches whose per-launch overhead at b40 exceeds fp32-simt's 18. geomean 26505.7->27124.4. fp32-SIMT is the best back-transform precision for shape 1. Reverting to fp32 (t6 best: shape1 1882us).

Restore best config: small-n (n<=200) via med split path (TC batched WY back-transform, t2 1.26x) + bisIters=32 (t6) + nt=512 + fp32 back-transform; square/2-slot/cluster/tf32 all OFF (measured net-negative). 39/39 VALID. Shape 1 confirmed 1890us (2460 baseline -> 1.30x), shape 2 6044 FLAT, geomean ~26633 (baseline 27021.7 -> 1.015x). Branch HEAD / best base. Kernel is barrier-bound (66%, ncu t6), un-hideable at 40 CTAs 1/SM.

Structured small-n bisIters sweep: 32->28 improves shape 1 1890->1865us fallback-free; 25 tips into mass fallback (2640us). 28 is the floor. 39/39 VALID. FINAL BEST: shape 1 2460->1865us = 1.32x (-24.2%); shape 2 6037 FLAT; all other shapes flat; geomean 27021.7->26470 = 1.021x. Win = med split path (TC WY back-transform, t2 1.26x) + bisIters 45->28. All multi-CTA/tensor-core/co-residency structural levers (t3-t10) measured net-negative: kernel is barrier-bound (66%) un-hideable at 40 CTAs 1/SM + tridiag-critical-path bound.

brief-114 (shape 1 n=176 b40 batch-parallelism). Forked/measured vs CURRENT BEST cf3d49aa (reset branch off it, not the stale CLI parent eef2bc186). BEST = t12 (2fab8e70): shape 1 2460->1865us = 1.32x (-24.2%), shape 2 (n=352) 6037 FLAT (no regression), all other 11 shapes flat, geomean 27021.7->26470 = 1.021x. 39/39 VALID, 'stream' absent, -O3.

DIAGNOSIS (trial-1 ncu, mega_eigh_k n=176 b40): occupancy-bound AND barrier-bound. Grid 40 CTAs = 0.27 waves/SM (108/148 SMs idle), Block Limit Shared Mem=1 (125KB FP32 V), Achieved Occupancy 12.5%, 2 warps/scheduler, No-Eligible 79.2%, 34.7% barrier stall. The in-kernel SIMT back-transform (~half the work) has no sibling warps to hide its per-column __syncthreads.

WHAT WON: (1) t2 route n<=200 through the med split path (mega_eigh_med_split): its TC batched-cuBLAS WY back-transform moves the back-transform off the single-CTA SIMT path onto the full GPU -> shape1 2460->1949us (1.26x). (2) t6/t12 small-n Sturm bisIters 45->28 (residual gate + twisted refinement tolerate coarser eigenvalues, fallback-free; 25 tips into mass fallback) -> 1949->1865us.

WHAT MEASURED NET-NEGATIVE (root causes, all 39/39 valid): (3) multi-CTA cluster tridiag C=2 PB in{1,4} (t3/t4): shape1 1949->2934/2918us -- cross-CTA cl.sync + global v/p staging + threadfence is DATA-MOVEMENT-bound (not sync-count-bound; PB didn't help), confirming brief-95 at n=176. (4) square-storage kernel (t5): 1949->2191 -- full-row trailing update = 2x the triangle-only rank-2 work, offsets the branch-free-indexing win. (5) named-barrier 2-slot co-residency (t8, 2 matrices/CTA on separate barriers): 1882->2492 -- the 2 slots share the same 4 schedulers so the named barrier waits on time-sliced warps (not hidden), and grid halves to 20 CTAs. (6) tf32 back-transform (t9): 1882->7877 mass fallback (too coarse over the WY product); tf32x3 (t10): 1882->2565 (18->54 GEMM launches).

The megakernel at b40 is barrier-bound (t6 ncu: 66% barrier, 10.6/16 cyc) and UN-HIDEABLE (40 CTAs 1/SM, no co-resident CTA; software co-residency shares the scheduler budget) + tridiag-critical-path bound (matrices already run in parallel across 40 SMs, so wall-clock = ONE matrix's serial tridiag). Adding CTAs adds cross-CTA sync/data-movement that exceeds the occupancy gain -> shape 1 is barrier-reachable only by cutting the tridiag CRITICAL PATH, not by filling idle SMs.

OPEN (unexplored, for the manager): (a) LATRD blocked-panel tridiag -- defer the trailing update to a batched TF32 GEMM (like the back-transform), cutting the ~174 trailing-update barriers to ~n/PB and moving that O(n^3) SIMT work to tensor cores; the one TC-tridiag lever I did NOT build (highest remaining upside, high effort). (b) parallelize the per-column symv dot-product across threads-per-row (warp-reduce) to shorten the O(n) inner loop on the critical path. (c) two committed-but-inactive kernels (mega_eigh_sq_split_k, mega_eigh_med_split2_k, flags off) could be pruned if this branch is selected. (d) shape 2 (n=352) shares the med path -- a small-n-style bisIters cut there was measured -2.6% in a probe but left at 45 (out of primary scope; safe to explore).

In-kernel LATRD blocked-panel tridiag (mega_eigh_med_blk, nbP=8): accumulate pb reflectors + w-vectors in SMEM w/ intra-panel compact-WY corrections (2k dots = ONE barrier via 2k threads x length-n serial sum), ONE trailing update per panel over the SMEM triangle. A stays SMEM-resident. 39/39 VALID, correct (2313us genuine, not fallback). Shape 1 1865->2313us REGRESSION (nbP=8), geomean 26470->26889, shape 2 FLAT. Per-column WY correction adds more work than the once-per-panel trailing update saves (brief-112 confirmed corrections dominate). Sweeping nbP.

LATRD blocked-panel nbP sweep {4,8,16}. 39/39 VALID at every nbP (correct, no fallback). Shape 1: nbP4 2326us, nbP8 2313us (best blocked), nbP16 2683us -- ALL worse than per-column med 1865us. Shape 2 FLAT. geomean nbP4 26911/nbP8 26889/nbP16 27191 vs 26470 best. DECISIVE: LATRD blocking does not beat per-column reduction at n=176/b40 -- WY correction + panel-start-A symv cost more than the once-per-panel trailing update saves (brief-112's finding confirmed for small-n). Trailing update was never the dominant per-column cost. Reverting to per-column best (t12) after profiling barrier-count/column.

Disable LATRD blocking (measured net-negative all nbP), restore per-column med best. ncu barrier map: blocked kernel barrier stall HIGHER (12.9/18.34=70%) than per-column (10.6/16.03=66%), kernel 1.86 vs 1.43ms, occupancy identical 25% (same 40 CTAs) -- intra-panel WY correction adds MORE per-column sync than the once-per-panel trailing update removes. Trailing update was never the dominant per-column cost; per-column Householder dependency chain is the true critical-path floor. Blocked kernel kept in-file inactive. RESTORED GLOBAL BEST: shape 1 1856us (2460 baseline -> 1.32x), shape 2 6046 FLAT, geomean 26484 (baseline 27021.7 -> 1.020x). 39/39 VALID.

brief-114 RESUMED (coordinator: LATRD blocked-panel lever). Built it in the n<=200 megakernel path; forked/measured vs the CURRENT BEST 2fab8e70 (my own prior final). RESULT: LATRD blocking is MEASURED net-negative at n=176/b40 -- does NOT beat the per-column 1865us. Final HEAD ad9da586 = per-column best restored (global best intact, blocked kernel kept in-file inactive as evidence).

BUILT: mega_eigh_med_blk_k -- in-kernel SMEM-resident LATRD. Accumulate pb<=nbP columns' Householder reflectors V + w-vectors W in SMEM via intra-panel compact-WY corrections (the 2*k correction dot-products done by 2k threads each one length-n serial sum = ONE barrier, an improvement over brief-112's 2k separate tree reductions), then ONE trailing update A-=VW^T+WV^T over the SMEM FP16 triangle per PANEL instead of per column. A stays SMEM-resident (unlike brief-112's global-A n=1024 kernel, which was the right call at n=1024 but wrong here). 39/39 VALID at every nbP, correct (genuine kernel runs, NOT masked by cuSOLVER fallback).

nb SWEEP (shape 1, vs per-column med 1865us): nbP=4 2326us, nbP=8 2313us (best blocked), nbP=16 2683us -- ALL regress. Shape 2 (n=352, per-col path, untouched) 6037-6046 FLAT throughout. geomean nbP4 26911/nbP8 26889/nbP16 27191 vs 26484 best.

BARRIER-COUNT/COLUMN MAP (coordinator's fallback ask -- ncu, shape 1): per-column med kernel 1.43ms, barrier stall 10.6 of 16.03 warp-cyc = 66%, occ 25%, No-Elig 75%. Blocked LATRD nbP=8: 1.86ms, barrier stall 12.9 of 18.34 = 70% (HIGHER), occ 25% (IDENTICAL, same 40 CTAs), No-Elig 78%. The blocking INCREASED the per-column barrier stall rather than cutting it: the intra-panel WY correction adds more synchronization points per column (corrected-column read + symv + correction-dot + p-correction barriers) than the once-per-panel trailing update removes; tensor-core-active % stayed ~0 (the trailing update is in-kernel SIMT here, not a GEMM -- and brief-112 measured the trailing GEMM is only ~5ms even at n=1024, so a GEMM form would not change the verdict).

VERDICT: shape 1's reduction is NOT profitably blockable at n=176/b40. The trailing update was NEVER the dominant per-column cost (the symv + the 2 reduction barriers are); blocking it cannot shorten the critical path. The per-column Householder dependency chain IS the true critical-path floor. This matches brief-112's independent n=1024 finding (corrections dominated; trailing GEMM 5ms) -- now confirmed for the small-n SMEM-resident case.

CUMULATIVE brief-114 (across both passes): shape 1 2460 (cf3d49aa) -> 1856us = 1.32x (-24.6%); shape 2 FLAT; all shapes flat; geomean 27021.7 -> 26484 = 1.020x. WINS: (1) route n<=200 through the med split path (TC batched WY back-transform, 1.26x); (2) small-n bisIters 45->28. NET-NEGATIVE structural levers all measured with root causes: multi-CTA cluster tridiag (cross-CTA data-movement), square storage (2x trailing update), named-barrier co-residency (shared scheduler budget), TC-precision back-transform (mass fallback / launch overhead), and now LATRD blocking (WY correction > trailing-update savings).

OPEN (unexplored): (a) parallelize the per-column symv dot-product across threads-per-row (warp-reduce) to shorten the O(n) inner loop that IS on the critical path -- the one per-column cost not yet attacked (risk: adds a reduction/column, and briefs 83/95 found sync-count reductions anti-correlate). (b) a fundamentally different eigensolver for n=176 (e.g. spectral D&C split into two ~88 sub-blocks) if split+merge undercuts the direct megakernel critical path -- not built. (c) five committed-but-inactive kernels now in-file (mega_eigh_sq_split_k, mega_eigh_med_split2_k, mega_eigh_med_blk_k + the cluster full-solve wiring, flags off) -- a simplify pass could prune ~580 lines if this branch is selected.
